summary.headline: Bosch Ltd Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 28.6% to INR61,641 mn and EBITDA 30.1% to INR8,028 mn, with H2 guided modest.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Jul-Sep 2026 was INR76,551 mn (up 28.2% YoY), with EBITDA of INR10,371 mn (up 23.2%), after including Bosch Chassis Systems India (RBIC) from 1 July 2026. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 13% in Q2 versus about 14% in the prior two quarters, as aluminium prices and a weaker rupee against the euro offset volume absorption. A one-time reversal of long-term service award provision (INR1,240 mn standalone, INR1,304 mn consolidated) sits in exceptional items and lifted reported PAT. Management guided to a more modest H2 on inflation, weak monsoon, tighter rates and a high base, and announced a 3:1 bonus issue and a split of INR10 shares into INR2 face value, subject to shareholder approval.

financial_highlights.change: -13.1% YoY; prior year included INR5,560 mn one-time gain on sale of Building Technologies businesses
-17.6% YoY; Q2 PAT +21.7% YoY incl. INR1,240 mn exceptional credit

segments.name: Mobility (standalone)
segments.commentary: Mobility grew 30.3% YoY in Q2 and 28% in H1, led by Powertrain Solutions, then two-wheeler and aftermarket. Consumer Goods (power tools) grew 17.1% in Q2 and 19% in H1.

segments.name: Powertrain Solutions
segments.commentary: Growth came from passenger cars, commercial vehicles and tractors in Q2. Management cites CAFE Phase 3 (effective April 2027) and CNG/ethanol/hybrid incentives as content-per-vehicle drivers.

segments.name: Two-Wheeler & Powersports
segments.commentary: Growth came from higher motorcycle production and value-added electronic functions. Electronic control modules passed 10 million cumulative units; ABS and engine management launched on a 160 cc motorcycle.

segments.name: Mobility Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Robust growth from OE spares, rotating machines, spark plugs, batteries and filters. Bosch workshop network crossed 5,000.

segments.name: RBIC (Bosch Chassis Systems India)
segments.commentary: Acquired 1 July 2026; FY26 revenue INR48,935 mn, EBITDA INR9,045 mn, PAT INR5,891 mn. Q2 EBITDA margin about 15.5% versus above 18% in FY26, hit by aluminium, ECU and forex costs and one-time ramp costs.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to be modest; Q3 FY27 seen as flat to modest growth on a high prior-year base, per management.
Management expects RBIC margins to remain pressured for about one more quarter before recovering toward earlier levels, with some raw-material costs to be recovered.
Management says margins are on an upward track on an aggregated basis, though it declined to give a specific margin target.
Depreciation timing effect of INR77.5 crore in H1 FY26 at RBIC is expected to reverse in later quarters.
CAFE Phase 3 effective April 2027; content-per-vehicle uplift not quantified and deferred to a later call.
TACO joint venture (Nashik) to start production mid-FY28; TSF joint venture (Chennai) towards end-FY28.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR350 crore, against roughly INR300 crore a year over the last three years; spend is seasonal and heaviest in Q3.
Most capex goes to plant and machinery, mainly upgrading existing production lines to meet volume.
RBIC plants at Chakan (Pune), Sanand (Gujarat) and Manesar (Haryana); Chakan has passed 20 million cumulative active safety units.
RBIC added ABS10M capacity for two-wheelers and started production of ESP10 in H1, which carried one-time costs.
Chennai power tools plant passed 20 million cumulative units.
demand_pricing: Passenger vehicle demand strong on low base and SUV preference; HCV, LCV and three-wheeler demand also strong in Q2.
Tractor demand weakened late in Q2 on uneven monsoon, though tractors still grew in Q2 per management.
Raw material inflation (mainly aluminium and ECUs) and INR depreciation against the euro weighed on margins; pass-through is contractual with time lags and some customers push back.
Management says it is trying to recover the full cost increase but cannot yet predict 100% recovery.
FX is passed through under contract for most customers; one customer is negotiation-based.
Standalone exports about 8-9% of sales on average, with Bosch's global network guided at 5-15% export per plant.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RBIC margins fall sharply, and how do pass-through and FX recovery work?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume absorption is the main driver; aluminium and forex on imported parts are the key cost headwinds. Recovery is contractual with a time lag, and full recovery is not assured given customer pushback.

qa_highlights.question: How should H2 demand be expected to trend sequentially, given festive retail and tractor weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed H2 will be modest, citing inflation, weak monsoon, rate tightening and a very high base. Q2 was a record quarter, so cyclicality is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR1,240 mn exceptional reversal, and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Bosch decided to stop the long-term service award globally. Eligible staff keep it until 31 December 2026, and the provision made for it is being reversed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RBIC capex and high ROCE model based on?
qa_highlights.answer: Lines are largely relocated from other Bosch plants and built modularly with heavy reuse, so capex per line is low. Management says current generations will look similar, but new generations may differ.

qa_highlights.question: How much RBIC purchases come from group entities and in foreign currency?
qa_highlights.answer: ECUs come from sister plant Bosch Automotive Electronics and will continue. Localisation of other content is ongoing and expected to rise over time.

qa_highlights.question: Will the parent restructuring or the China-to-India sourcing shift affect Bosch Limited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the parent's mobility division spin-off has no impact on Bosch Limited. India exports are about 8-9%, and any shift in sourcing is still being assessed with the parent.

risks_watch: Aluminium and ECU prices plus INR/EUR forex, with recovery lagging and not fully assured.
H2 FY27 demand softness in tractors and possibly other segments after a record Q2 and a high base.
Standalone EBITDA margin of about 13% in Q2 versus about 14% in prior quarters; management gave no numerical target.
RBIC EBITDA margin trajectory and whether the one-time ramp costs and depreciation timing reverse next quarter.
Revenue and EBITDA growth of 20-30% has not translated into PAT growth after one-time items.
Share bonus and split need shareholder approval; record date still to be set.
EV revenue salience and order book were not disclosed; the JV is still being set up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and the festive quarter, but cautious on H2, citing inflation, weak monsoon and rate tightening. Evasive on specifics: it declined to quantify CAFE 3 content, margin targets, EV exposure and full cost pass-through.
key_quotes: A little more modest second half is likely outcome as we go forward.
We are trying to recuperate the whole amount.
So, the current situation, for your information, is that we also have an export number of maybe 8 percent or 9 percent on an average from India.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin about 13% in Q2 versus about 14% in prior two quarters; RBIC Q2 margin about 15.5% vs above 18% in FY26, with management saying margins are on an upward track on an aggregated basis but giving no numeric target and full aluminium/forex recovery not assured.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: TACO JV (Nashik) to start production mid-FY28 and TSF JV (Chennai) towards end-FY28, both under construction; H1 FY27 capex about INR350 crore is mainly line upgrades, not new plants, so no major new capacity comes live in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided Q3 FY27 flat to modest growth on a high prior-year base and H2 'a little more modest', after Q2 standalone revenue rose 28.6% to INR61,641 mn; tractor demand weakened late in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure disclosed; H1 FY27 capex about INR350 crore is only modestly above the roughly INR300 crore annual run-rate, and management is describing line upgrades rather than a new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided H2 FY27 to be more modest on inflation, weak monsoon, rate tightening and a high base, with no numeric revenue guidance offered.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management has already signalled a more modest H2 and flat-to-modest Q3 two-wheeler growth against a high base, and RBIC margins are expected to stay pressured for about one more quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ABS and engine management launched on a 160 cc motorcycle and ESP10 started at RBIC in H1, but no new product revenue sizing was disclosed and EV exposure was not quantified.

rows.label: Raw material and FX pass-through recovery
rows.why: Pass-through is contractual with time lags for most customers and one is negotiation-based; management says it is trying to recover the full cost increase but cannot predict 100% recovery, against aluminium and euro headwinds.

rows.label: 3:1 bonus issue and INR10 to INR2 face value split
rows.why: Announced on this call and subject to shareholder approval, with record date still to be set; it changes share count and per-share optics but not fundamentals.

rows.label: CAFE Phase 3 content-per-vehicle uplift
rows.why: CAFE Phase 3 is effective April 2027 and Powertrain Solutions drove Q2 growth, but management did not quantify the content uplift and deferred it to a later call.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record Q2 volume and festive demand but cautious on H2, citing inflation, weak monsoon and rate tightening, and it avoided quantifying margin targets, CAFE 3 content and full cost pass-through.
